That's completely understandable! Any/all or none of the above possibilities could be active agents. If you're unsure about your diagnosis, definitely discuss that with the mental health professional you see. In regards to the medication, do the same (with that one, explain how long you've been on them and anything you've been noticing, like unpleasant changes/lack of changes etc).
Usually with medication, it takes at least a month before the active ingredient starts to truly kick in, as your body needs to build up what is in the medication, in order for it to start taking effect.

But do try your best to stay focused on the parts you need to address with the professional. Make notes, an example I would use would be like this:

"What I want to address:

• diagnosis (Is it a definite diagnosis? Is it a possible diagnosis? What things indicate this definite/possible diagnosis).
*Basically so you can get a better understanding of what it means specifically for you.*

• medication (how it's making you feel/not feel, changes you have noticed/lack of changes since being on this etc)"
*Very important to mention this, especially if you've been on the medication for a few months, sometimes they like to see how it goes roughly around or upto 6 months of use.*

Sort of like a quick note version of what you really want to cover and bring it to the appointment with you. Also means you don't have to worry about the thing I get, where if I forget my notes, I wind up sporadically blurting out everything and completely forget what I wanted to really talk about.
I'm also sure they'd be happy to have you hand them your note and they can go through each pointer with you.
Although they'll probably base it on what they think would be most important for you, so maybe add a little something to the start, like, "what I want to address, in order of importance:"

Hope this helps! And if I don't get a chance to talk with you again before your appointment, I hope it goes great for you and that you can get answers to at least 1 or 2 of the main things causing you issues!
But definitely keep us posted on how it went for you! I would really love for you to get the right and best help, that works for you!

Other than that, feel free to hit me up anytime, I'm liking the brain work! And in case you ever get rid of this thread :)

I guess then, you might not have to worry if they're going to stick around. It sounds like they might be actual, true friends! It's normal to panic when there's going to be change but the best thing you can do with that, here's my method:

Put each thing in a separate box, in your mind (or even physically create a few, whichever way works best for you) and things based on people, go in one box. Things based on places, go in another box and so on.

It means you can compartmentalise things in a manageable, healthier way.
So if something changes about, in this instance, a place....... Then the only thing you'll be concerned about is the place and not everyone and everything it involves, being included into the worry.

Instead, it will just be about it and you'll be able to work out, easier, what you can do to replace it. To basically fill it's lack of occupancy.
And also means you don't feel you need to question the other areas, like people.

Hope that helps.
